newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Tietmeyer says hears of no new gold sale plans.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says hears of no new gold sale plans.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said he had heard of no central banks planning new gold sales since Switzerland announced last week that it planned to put some reserve gold on the market in the longer-term.
Tietmeyer said the issue of central bank gold reserves was not discussed among Group of 10 (G10) central bank governors on Monday at the Bank for International Settlements here.
Tietmeyer was speaking to reporters after the regular monthly meeting of G10 central bank governors, of which he is chairman.
"I haven't heard anybody who has indicated that he will do gold sales," Tietmeyer said.
Tietmeyer was responding to a question from reporters about whether central banks were more willing to sell gold reserves after the Swiss announcement last week.

The Swiss government last Wednesday said it planned to revalue Swiss National Bank gold reserves and give seven billion Swiss francs in reserve gold to a proposed humanitarian foundation, which would sell the gold gradually over a period of up to 10 years.
The Swiss government's proposal must still be approved by parliament and by voters in a referendum sometime in 1998. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
